pr_title: Fix slider input handling potentially being offset after composer area resize
pr_comments:
Tests are failing because of snaking. The drawable slider's bounds cannot be relied on for editor selection when snaking is enabled, because the underlying drawable path is changing. That broke quick-deletion in that test there (you can only delete the slider by clicking on its head in the current state of things).

Not sure how to handle that but honestly any solution to this would probably be quite close to reverting to that `AlwaysPresent = true` variant, because it looks like that the snaking issue is what `ManualSliderBody` was solving in the first place. So I'd probably do just that.

issue_context.title: (Slider) Paths are reporting incorrect `ReceivePositionalInputAt` in some cases
issue_context.body:
When entering the editor with a slider already on screen, clicking the blueprint doesn't work. This is due to the animation that plays when entering (not sure we want this animation but let's ignore that), which shifts the composer and its children downwards. The path is still reporting as if it is at the pre-transform location.

I've traced this down to framework's `Path`. It resolves after clicking the blueprint.

![20210503 184403 (JetBrains Rider)](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/116862319-89380880-ac3f-11eb-88cf-b7e4f1512484.png)


https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/191335/116862388-9fde5f80-ac3f-11eb-8a67-46ce399a3cc7.mp4

This can also be reproduced by toggling the timeline "Control Points" display mode, causing a resize of the playfield.
comments:
I think framework fix is not required.
Because `SliderBodyPiece` is always transparent, `IsPresent` is `false` and the body piece is not updated (not sure what exactly the mechanism of this is).
Setting `AlwaysPresent = true` will resolve the issue.
Setting `AlwaysPresent` unconditionally should be an absolute last resort.

Right, this is making a whole lot more sense now. I was sure that the `BodyPiece` reference was one inside the `DrawableSlider`, but as it turns out it's part of the blueprint.

I think we should be checking against the `DrawableSlider` instead.

> Setting `AlwaysPresent` unconditionally should be an absolute last resort.

I think it actually makes sense here, as it's a tightly coupled component with its direct parent relying on it for input handling.
